full_judgment: 17. After going through the judgment of the learned Appellate Judge, I find that he has very clearly and vividly discussed about the point of limitation whereas Mr Shaheed Alam the learned Advocate for the petitioners argued this point that the learned Appellate Judge did not discuss at all about the point of limitation as on point of limitation the suit was not maintainable and, as such, the finding of the learned Trial Judge is correct but after going through the judgment of the learned Appellate Judge I do not find any truth or substances in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner Mr Shaheed Alam on his first point. In respect of second point of his submission that has been placed by Mr Shaheed Alam that remedy of the plaintiff opposite parties lies in filing of a partition suit to get their share in the disputed plot of land if they can prove their title and since their claim is only 18 decimals of land out of 3.27 acres. On this point after going through the plaint of the plaintiff I find that the claimed land of the plaintiff has been very specifically and properly described in the schedule of the plaint, inasmuch as the boundary of 18 decimals of land has also been described in the plaint. Apart from this I have gone through the schedule of the' title deeds of purchase by the mother of the plaintiffs being of the year 1943 and 1950 and also in the schedule of both the deeds I find that the schedule as given in the plaint is exactly right that of the schedule given in the title deeds. Moreover, the local investigation report submitted by the learned Advocate Commissioner also speaks of truth of claim of the plaintiff and the learned Appellate Judge has very consciously taken into consideration this aspect of the case and thus arrived at his decision for decreeing the suit. As such the citation being the case reported in 41 DLR (AD) 106 referred to by Mr Shaheed Alam is not coming to any help to his case because the finding of our Lordships in the Appellate Division could have been attracted in this case if the claimed land of the plaintiffs were vague and unspecified and without giving proper boundary and exact location. For this reason, I am unable to accept the contention of second submission of Mr Shaheed Alam and after going through the impugned judgment and the evidences-on-record, I do not find any misreading or non-reading of evidences or misconstruction of any papers or document by the learned Appellate Judge. The impugned judgment, in my opinion, is well reasoned and appreciable judgment strictly in adherence to the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure which deserves to be upheld. As such, I do not find any merit in the Rule.
